text: Chapter 1's loop doesn't end at "made a change." It ends at verify — measuring again and confirming the exact bottleneck moved, without quietly breaking something else.

Running the exact same test — TrailWorks Co-op, CustomerID 48213 — with statistics on: before, twenty-eight thousand milliseconds and a hundred eighteen thousand logical reads, with the Key Lookup running eighteen thousand four hundred times. After, eighty-five milliseconds, three hundred fifty logical reads, and no Key Lookup operator in the plan at all — just a single covered Index Seek.

Chapter 1 warned against declaring victory off one number. Checking wait stats during the next ten AM to two PM window shows PAGEIOLATCH_SH attributable to this query has dropped to essentially nothing. Plan, metrics, and waits all agree — that's what makes this verified, not just lucky-looking.

Lesson one's guide warned about a fix that helps reads while hurting writes. But dropping the redundant old index means the table maintains the same number of nonclustered indexes as before — just one wider one instead of a narrow one. Checking index usage stats and Query Store confirms no write-side regression.
Four independent confirmations — plan, metrics, waits, and no collateral damage — not one lucky number. Next up: writing this up for the team.
